records.reason: Molecule m167 at intermediate strength and high loading has wide predicted V1/V2 ranges and high CW distance. It probes a carbonyl-rich, fluorinated family region with little local calibration.
The m208 condition has very broad predicted widths and high CW distance. It is a strong probe for whether an iodine phenol-like scaffold follows the late-tail branch or remains compact.
This stronger, higher-loading m208 point extends the same scaffold response into a regime where the model predicts a large V2 range, allowing a condition-response slope to be learned.
This m178 intermediate-strength point bridges measured m178 behavior at 10/1 (634f21e11a8442494ce3) and 50/1 (0c5c35afb3a24375c153), helping learn the transition rather than only another endpoint.
A lower-strength m117 point with high CW distance tests the onset and finish of a multifunctional aldehyde/phenol scaffold before the late behavior seen at 50/1 in d9c8c8af50a10bf07765.
This high-strength, high-loading m117 point complements the lower-strength m117 probe and tests whether the predicted finish tail grows smoothly or appears after a scaffold-specific transition.
At fixed 10/1 strength, this m191 row changes loading relative to the measured 50-ul point b0802294da4fd71d0f9d. Its broad V2 range directly tests loading effects in a dialdehyde-like scaffold.

The m173 high-loading condition has an unusually wide predicted range. It extends the measured m173 5/1 response in 1e971da91b3a8229f0e0 toward stronger solvent and can separate a genuine acid-related tail from extrapolation.

This m66 point tests a stronger-solvent condition in a heteroaromatic carbonyl family where the measured 2/1 row 4659b6752f23c0b85f08 already shows substantial retention. It can calibrate the strength slope and V2 tail.

The m107 2/1 condition has large model widths and high CW distance. It probes whether the observed long finish at 1/1 and high loading in b7953b4cf8c561ff4cfe persists after changing strength and loading.
This compact predicted m107 low-strength anchor paired with the broader m107 regime tests whether the apparent tail is caused by solvent strength, loading, or a scaffold-level offset.
The m141 2/1 point has high CW distance and a broad predicted V2 range. It provides a lower-strength anchor for the severe heteroaromatic behavior measured at 10/1 in 7fb4f90753d40dd25be0.
This matched m141 condition changes loading relative to the other m141 probe, allowing the model to distinguish a loading-driven finish expansion from a solvent-strength transition.
A low-strength m211 anchor is useful before the very late behavior measured at 50/1 in 449b809e4efaaf2af86a. It constrains where the heteroaromatic transition begins.
This low-strength m177, high-loading point supplies a missing local anchor for a scaffold whose measured labels show modest onset but potentially extreme finish tails at stronger conditions.
The m177 5/1 counterpart tests the first strength increment before the measured 20/1 and 50/1 tails in 5e276c1730fc0a9deba7 and b514312eda7950cdcf1c.
This m92 EA condition fills an intermediate-strength point in a solvent-response family that includes measured EA rows such as 9bbd36c8b484b5609808 and 50e113fcc37184809670.
The m92 50/1 EA row changes loading relative to the measured 50/1, 150-ul point 9bbd36c8b484b5609808. Its broad predicted range directly tests loading effects on the finish tail.
This m79 high-strength DCM point tests whether the unusual high-strength behavior seen under PE in 9f2c033ca3b34b46ac99 transfers across mobile-phase composition.
A low-strength m79 control paired with the high-strength probe establishes whether this donor-free scaffold has a genuine strength transition or remains an ordinary compact row.

The m12 condition adds a higher-loading, intermediate-strength point to measured m12 behavior in c8f65df578125328ba0e and 418a798336105bff06e0, testing whether its broad finish is strength- or loading-dependent.
This high-strength m12 row probes the donor-free aromatic exception branch. It helps distinguish a real late tail from the ordinary compact controls supported by 0f756a58174e946b976a.
The m44 20/1 point has a broad predicted finish range and lower loading than the measured 1/1 point d9a6c373815a35cd0e05. It tests strength and loading effects in a routine ketone family.
This m40 intermediate-strength, high-loading point bridges ordinary behavior and the late high-strength response measured at 50/1 in 8b9ff1a26d840aaa6a49.
A second m44 point at 50/1 and low loading tests whether the wide predicted finish is a real high-strength tail or an uncertainty artifact, complementing the intermediate-strength m44 probe.
The m26 20/1 condition probes carbonyl-rich behavior at high loading, extending the measured 10/1 m26 response in ba0d2f91eb0b005857f8 toward a possible late branch.

This m104 condition has modest predicted widths but belongs to a family with a measured high-strength compact point 302e458c5ed2285ca328. It tests whether the apparent family response changes across strength.
A low-strength m208 anchor is needed to interpret the two broad high-strength m208 candidates and to determine whether the tail is activated by solvent strength or is scaffold-intrinsic.
This compact predicted m74 row is a routine PE control with low CW distance. It protects central-distribution accuracy while late-retention repairs are learned elsewhere.
The m57 donor-free, halogenated row is a compact high-strength control and complements the measured compact m57 point 0f756a58174e946b976a.
This low-strength m25 control has very small predicted width and low CW distance, providing an ordinary ester-like anchor against indiscriminate tail correction.
The compact m77 low-strength condition is a chemically distinct ordinary control. It helps check whether broad V2 corrections spill into simple donor-free ester chemistry.

hypotheses.content: Solvent-strength response and onset/finish coupling remain scaffold-specific, with transition locations and slopes that cannot be represented reliably by one global PE/EA trend.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local strength anchors can teach scaffold-conditioned transitions and slopes for both V1 and V2, reducing inappropriate global solvent corrections.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do transition locations transfer within functional-group families, or must they remain scaffold-specific?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and loading-solvent volume alter V1 and V2 differently across scaffolds, so mass alone is insufficient as a universal loading correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading contrasts help separate amount-driven onset shifts from finish-tail expansion instead of folding both into solvent or molecular descriptors.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed molecule and PE/EA ratio, does loading primarily shift onset, expand finish, or change both in a scaffold-dependent way?

hypotheses.content: V2 and interval width require direct local calibration; predicted quantile width is useful for finding probes but is not a generally calibrated estimate of finish-tail behavior.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Direct V2 labels across compact and broad predicted regimes teach when a wide interval reflects a real chromatographic tail.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can structural descriptors predict finish width across families, or are local scaffold-condition anchors required?

hypotheses.content: Late-retention failures cluster across heteroatom-rich, carbonyl-rich, heteroaromatic, and multifunctional scaffolds, but their transition locations remain local.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Family-diverse tail probes can teach transferable structural signals while preserving family-specific transition locations.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which local structural environments best identify a scaffold's transition into late V2 behavior?

hypotheses.content: Donor-free, halogenated, and compact acceptor-only rows are not one uniform behavior class; ordinary controls are needed alongside difficult rows to prevent indiscriminate tail correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Chemically distinct compact controls protect overall Row-distribution accuracy while allowing exceptions to be learned locally.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which donor-free and acceptor-only environments remain compact across strength and loading regimes, and which are genuine exceptions?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes strengthened the local-response interpretation. m125 spans compact low-strength behavior in e7ed7ca4a53258b73ba2, a large intermediate-strength finish in 69b09343d0b9995c3ae4, and a late high-strength response in 74cf50c6ec476a394b01. The m177 outcomes b514312eda7950cdcf1c, 5e276c1730fc0a9deba7, and 5442611ea6789d42bc86 show that V2 tails can change dramatically while V1 changes modestly or in the opposite direction. m96 again separates compact and late regimes: 914cbf3bfe7468210e0e is compact while 5bad82a6cffd60e7a6c9 is a broad-tail point. The large errors for 2cf789c87f7c6325c020 and 2e6a6b82f8ddb64a9011 support retaining ordinary controls and testing exceptions locally.
batch_rationale: The batch concentrates labels where the current model is most likely to generalize poorly: high-CW and wide-range probes cover multifunctional, heteroaromatic, carbonyl-rich, and donor-rich tail families; paired points for m117, m177, m92, m79, m12, m44, m208, and m107 probe response curves and loading effects; and four compact controls anchor the ordinary central distribution. The combination should improve residual correction for V1 and V2, teach when predicted width corresponds to a real finish tail, and reduce spillover of late-family repairs into chemically ordinary rows.
